claims.sentence: Tension-type headache typically causes a pressing or tightening pain on both sides of the head, and the area can feel tender to the touch.
claims.evidence: MedlinePlus: dull pressure, tight band; leaflet: both sides. 'Tender to touch' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: Tension-type headache typically causes a dull, pressing or tight-band pain felt on both sides of the head.

claims.sentence: NICE describes the pain as mild to moderate and not made worse by routine activity.
claims.evidence: Mild-to-moderate and not worsened by daily activity came from an NHS-linked leaflet, not retrieved NICE text.
claims.newSentence: An NHS-linked self-care leaflet describes tension-type headache as mild to moderate and not made worse by ordinary daily activity.

claims.sentence: The NHS says a tension headache is commonly felt for 30 minutes to several hours, but it can last for days.
claims.evidence: NHS page: at least 30 minutes, can last several days. 'Several hours' came from trust leaflets.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says tension headaches last at least 30 minutes and can last for several days.

claims.sentence: MedlinePlus says it usually does not come with nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light and sound.
claims.evidence: MedlinePlus: usually no nausea or vomiting; light/sound not retrieved from it. NINDS says tension-type headache may involve light or sound sensitivity.
claims.newSentence: MedlinePlus says tension headaches usually do not cause nausea or vomiting.

claims.sentence: NICE describes migraine as a headache that is usually throbbing or pulsating, often moderate to severe, and that can be on one side or both.
claims.evidence: Moderate-to-severe, one or both sides, from leaflet; NICE diagnostic text not retrieved; 'usually throbbing' only from NHS 111 Wales.
claims.newSentence: An NHS-linked self-care leaflet describes migraine as usually moderate to severe, on one or both sides of the head, and it can be made worse by ordinary daily activity.

claims.sentence: Nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound are common.
claims.evidence: NHS migraine page lists feeling/being sick and sensitivity to light and sound as main symptoms.

claims.sentence: Attacks typically last for hours, and some people have an aura, a set of temporary symptoms such as visual disturbance, before the headache starts.
claims.evidence: NHS migraine page: attacks usually last 4 hours to 3 days; aura includes zigzag lines/flashing lights, numbness etc.

claims.sentence: For tension-type headache, the NHS says over-the-counter painkillers such as paracetamol and ibuprofen can help, along with relaxation, exercise and good sleep and posture habits.
claims.evidence: NICE: consider aspirin, paracetamol or NSAID for TTH. NHS: relaxation activities. Exercise, sleep, posture not retrieved; NHS-attribution of painkillers came from a leaflet.
claims.newSentence: For tension-type headache, NICE advises considering aspirin, paracetamol or an NSAID for the acute treatment, and the NHS mentions activities that help you relax.

claims.sentence: A GP may discuss a preventive medicine for frequent headaches.
claims.evidence: Not retrieved for TTH; NICE MOH info says preventive treatment for the underlying headache may be offered with withdrawal.
claims.newSentence: NICE says treatment to help prevent the underlying headache may be offered alongside stopping the medicines that are causing medication-overuse headache.

claims.sentence: For migraine, NICE advises that acute treatment is most effective when started early.
claims.evidence: NHS migraine page says take painkillers as soon as headache starts; NICE 'most effective early' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The NHS migraine page advises taking painkillers as soon as the headache starts.

claims.sentence: It recommends a triptan combined with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug or paracetamol, with the choice made by the clinician.
claims.evidence: NICE: offer oral triptan with NSAID, or with paracetamol. 'Choice made by clinician' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: For the acute treatment of migraine, NICE advises offering an oral triptan together with an NSAID, or an oral triptan together with paracetamol.

claims.sentence: Taking painkillers or triptans too often can cause medication-overuse headache, so a GP can advise on how often is appropriate.
claims.evidence: MOH cause stated in a trust leaflet; NICE: treated by stopping medicines. 'GP can advise how often' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: Taking painkillers or triptans too often can cause medication-overuse headache, which NICE says is treated by stopping the medicines, with advice from a healthcare professional.

claims.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E for a sudden, extremely painful headache, a headache after a serious head injury, sudden problems with speech or memory, loss of vision, drowsiness or confusion, or a high temperature with other signs of meningitis such as a stiff neck or a rash.
claims.evidence: NHS Headaches page lists sudden extremely painful onset, head injury, loss of vision, confusion/drowsiness, seizure, numbness/weakness, non-fading rash. Speech/memory problems and fever with stiff neck came only from hospital leaflets.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E for a sudden and extremely painful headache, a headache after a head injury, loss of vision, confusion or drowsiness, a seizure, new numbness or weakness, or a rash that does not fade under a glass.

claims.sentence: These signs can mean a serious condition, and getting help promptly matters.
claims.evidence: General statement, harmless.

claims.sentence: A GP appointment is the route when headaches are frequent or severe, when painkillers are not helping, or when headaches affect work or daily life.
claims.evidence: NHS: see GP if headaches several times a week or severe, or painkillers/relaxation do not help. 'Affect work or daily life' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP if headaches happen several times a week or are severe, or if painkillers and relaxing activities do not help.

claims.sentence: A GP can look for other causes, review any painkillers being taken and discuss preventive treatment where it is suitable.
claims.evidence: No retrieved text on what a GP will review or offer.

claims.sentence: The site's page on headache sets out causes and warning signs in more detail.
claims.evidence: Meta pointer to site page, harmless.

claims.sentence: Tension-type headache usually causes a pressing or tightening pain on both sides of the head, with mild to moderate severity.
claims.evidence: MedlinePlus dull pressure/tight band; leaflet mild-moderate both sides.

claims.sentence: Migraine is often a throbbing pain that can be moderate to severe, with nausea, vomiting and sensitivity to light and sound.
claims.evidence: NHS migraine symptoms; moderate-severe from leaflet; throbbing from NHS 111 Wales.

claims.sentence: Some people have an aura before a migraine, and attacks last longer than a typical tension headache.
claims.evidence: NHS migraine: aura and 4h-3 days vs TTH 30 min up to days.

claims.sentence: Painkillers help both, but frequent use of painkillers can itself cause headaches.
claims.evidence: NICE acute treatment for both; trust leaflet on medication-overuse headache.

claims.sentence: A sudden, extremely painful headache, or a headache with confusion, vision loss or a stiff neck and high temperature, needs 999 or A&E.
claims.evidence: Fever with stiff neck not on retrieved NHS 999 list; remaining items are.
claims.newSentence: A sudden, extremely painful headache, or a headache with loss of vision, confusion or drowsiness, or a rash that does not fade under a glass, needs 999 or A&E.

claims.sentence: Tension headache is usually a dull, tight pressure on both sides of the head, while migraine often throbs and brings nausea or sensitivity to light.
claims.evidence: Supported by MedlinePlus, leaflet and NHS migraine page.

notes: Retrieval did not surface NICE CG150 diagnostic feature text or the NHS Headaches page 999 list verbatim in full; mild-moderate/both-sides/throbbing descriptions rest on an NHS-linked Nottinghamshire leaflet and NHS 111 Wales, not NICE. Verify the 999 list against nhs.uk/symptoms/headaches before publishing. NINDS says tension-type headache may involve light or sound sensitivity, so avoid saying it never does.
